topic: Central Asia fintech routing risk case packet
jurisdiction: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Caspian routes, UAE-linked trade exposure; sanctions and AML implications for a European fintech

claims.claim: Foreign financial institutions and third-country actors can face sanctions risk when supporting Russia's war economy, military-industrial base, alternative payment mechanisms, or sanctions-evasion schemes.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury - As Russia Completes Transition to a Full War Economy, Treasury Takes Sweeping Aim at Foundational Financial Infrastructure and Access to Third Country Support
supports: Third-country support and Russia war-economy risk pattern
Risk relevance of foundational financial infrastructure
limits: Does not assess any customer, bank, counterparty, transaction, route, or goods shipment in this case packet
Operational use requires current sanctions-list checks and qualified review

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury - Treasury Disrupts Russia's Sanctions Evasion Schemes
supports: Regional financial-node relevance when tied to evasion activity
limits: Does not establish that any prospective fintech customer is illicit
The packet does not perform sanctions screening

claims.claim: Payment connectivity and Russia-linked financial messaging can be a specific risk channel for foreign financial institutions.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury - Treasury Sanctions Gazprombank and Takes Additional Steps to Curtail Russia's Use of the International Financial System
limits: Does not evaluate this fictional fintech's actual payment rails
Bank-specific exposure requires current operational data

claims.claim: Caspian / Middle Corridor routing is commercially legitimate and strategically important, but route growth can increase review burden when goods, counterparties, end-users, or route changes are poorly explained.

sources.name: World Bank - Middle Corridor through Central Asia, Caucasus Can Boost Trade, Connectivity and Supply Chain Resilience
limits: Supports corridor legitimacy and growth context, not transaction-level sanctions or AML risk

sources.name: World Bank - World Bank Support to Enhance Rail Connectivity and Logistics in Kazakhstan
supports: Kazakhstan rail and logistics connectivity context
limits: Does not assess specific routes, shippers, vessels, banks, or customers

claims.claim: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan AML/CFT evaluation context is relevant to fintech onboarding design.

sources.name: FATF - Kazakhstan's measures to combat money laundering and terrorist financing
supports: Relevance of AML/CFT controls and effectiveness context
limits: Does not establish onboarding risk for a specific Kazakh customer
Does not replace customer-level due diligence

sources.name: Central Bank of Uzbekistan - EAG and the Mutual Evaluation of Uzbekistan
limits: Does not establish onboarding risk for a specific Uzbek customer
Does not replace transaction monitoring or legal review

claims.claim: UAE-linked counterparties are not inherently high risk, but hub intermediation can raise review burden when combined with sensitive goods, opaque ownership, Russia/Iran adjacency, or weak commercial rationale.

sources.name: FATF - Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring, 23 February 2024
supports: UAE was no longer subject to increased monitoring as of the FATF update
Areas previously requiring action included legal-person abuse, FIU capacity, ML investigations, and targeted financial sanctions implementation
limits: Does not assess any UAE-linked counterparty in this fictional scenario
Intermediation risk framing is analyst inference from hub exposure and sanctions/AML context

claims.claim: The recommended posture is conditional expansion with segment-level enhanced due diligence rather than unrestricted launch.
basis: Synthesizes the supported and partially supported claims above
Depends on assumptions about incomplete UBO records, goods-classification uncertainty, Caspian-connected routes, UAE-linked counterparties, and payment-rail sensitivity
limits: Not legal, compliance, sanctions, AML, investment, or operational advice
Could change materially with real customer data and qualified review

unsupported_claims: Any conclusion about a real customer, counterparty, bank, payment provider, route, vessel, owner, or transaction
Any claim that the fictional fintech's proposed onboarding portfolio is compliant or non-compliant
Any claim that a named party should be approved, rejected, blocked, or reported
source_plan: Current OFAC, EU, UK, UN, and relevant national sanctions-list checks
Current export-control list checks for actual goods categories and HS codes
Correspondent-bank feedback and risk appetite documentation
Route, vessel, logistics-provider, and end-user documentation
Qualified sanctions, AML, export-control, and legal review
